name: VARoleEditorTeamUpdateAnnouncement

custom.system_prompt: Meghan needs to announce a change to the team's testing process, and her draft buries the actual change under a long explanation of why it's needed. She asks Sigma to help make it clear and scannable. Sigma restructures for clarity without changing the content.

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Meghan needs to announce a change to the team's testing process, but her draft buries the actual change under a long explanation of why it's needed before ever stating what's changing. She asks Sigma to help make it clear and scannable. Sigma identifies the structural issue and proposes leading with the change itself, followed by rationale, preserving all the actual content. Keep every line short and natural — the opening line already addresses Sigma directly.

variations.context: Solo editing of a process-change announcement that buries the actual change under justification

setting.mood: Focused, wants the team to actually read and understand this
setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through a writing task with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: Meghan cares a lot about the reasoning behind the change and wrote it in the order she thought of it, not the order a reader needs

scenario_template.topic: Meghan addresses Sigma directly in her first line, describing the draft's problem — e.g. 'Sigma, I need to announce a testing process change but my draft buries the actual change under a long explanation. Help me make this scannable.' One short turn, straight to Sigma.
scenario_template.note: The draft's problem and the ask arrive together.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks her to state the actual change in one sentence, to use as the anchor for the restructured announcement.
scenario_template.note: Meghan's answer should be a clean, specific statement of the change.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma points out that her draft has four sentences of rationale before the actual change appears in sentence five, naming the specific structural issue.
scenario_template.note: References the actual structure of her draft.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proposes a restructured version leading with the change, followed by a brief rationale, preserving all her actual content and reasoning.
scenario_template.note: Nothing cut in substance, just reordered for scannability.

scenario_template.topic: Meghan reacts, satisfied the team will actually read this now, ready to send it. Keep this realistic — brisk and practical.

user1.name: Meghan
user1.role: Detail-oriented, methodical QA engineer, restructuring a process-change announcement that buries the change itself. Speaks in short, precise sentences. Ends satisfied and practical, ready to send.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Editor. Restructures a workplace announcement to lead with the actual change before rationale, preserving all content. Identifies the specific structural issue in the actual draft rather than generic writing advice.

conversation_structure: The opening line already addresses Sigma directly, describing the draft's specific structural problem
Sigma anchors the rewrite on a one-sentence statement of the actual change
Sigma names the specific structural issue (rationale before change) in the actual draft
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution preserves all content while reordering for scannability
assistant_behavior: Sigma preserves all the user's actual content and reasoning; it reorders, not cuts substance
Sigma's feedback is specific to the actual draft
